meta.description: Assigns taxonomy to amplicon ASVs/OTUs (16S, ITS, 18S) with a classifier conditioned on a reference database and primer region - DADA2 assignTaxonomy + addSpecies (RDP naive Bayes), DECIPHER IDTAXA, and QIIME2 q2-feature-classifier (classify-sklearn naive Bayes, classify-consensus-vsearch alignment-consensus).
meta.re_audit_of: F:/OpenScience/audits/_pre-fix-20260919c/bio-microbiome-taxonomy-assignment (pre-fix score 87, Reject, Skill Veto T3 -- IdTaxa() non-determinism)
meta.auditor_note: Fourth independent agent on this Skill (original auditor, fixer x2, re-auditor, now this re-re-auditor). Skill Veto T3 has fired on the two prior audit passes; this pass verifies it on data none of the prior three passes used.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 11 inputs (9 regression + 2 new) used real tools (DADA2 1.34.0, DECIPHER 3.2.0, QIIME2 2024.10.1) against real reference data (SILVA 138 QIIME2 artifacts) and real ASVs (770 sequences denoised from the public moving-pictures dataset). Inputs 10-11 additionally used a freshly-drawn, independent 18,000-sequence real SILVA-138 subsample (seed 4242, size and seed never used by the original auditor, either fixer, or the prior re-auditor -- who used 8k/30k/60k/380k/5k draws). No fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, p-values, or effect sizes anywhere.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive claims about an individual anywhere; scope remains community/environmental marker-gene taxonomy. Unchanged from all prior passes.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy found. This pass's own finding (assignTaxonomy's multithread=FALSE does not deliver full bitwise identity at every rank, see determinism note) is an engineering precision gap in a code comment, not a methodological error, and is scored under Skill Veto / static criteria rather than here.

code_usability.detail: All code across all 11 inputs executed without syntax errors and no missing-dependency failures in the reused microbiome-metagenomics-analyst environment. Every finding in this re-audit was discovered by code that ran to completion and produced a checked, non-trivial result (identical() and all.equal() comparisons, per-rank diff counts) -- never an exit-code-only claim.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness and correctness: all three stochastic calls in this Skill (assignTaxonomy, LearnTaxa, IdTaxa) are now seeded and independently reproduced on a data slice none of the prior three passes used (18,000-sequence SILVA-138 subsample, seed 4242): LearnTaxa() seeded twice gives identical() trainingSet objects; unseeded gives a different one (confirms genuine stochasticity, not a no-op fix). IdTaxa() seeded is identical() across 2 runs in BOTH single- and multi-threaded configurations, and the multithreaded output is even identical() to the single-threaded output -- a stronger determinism result than the Skill claims. One point held back: this re-audit found the fix log's/SKILL.md comment's claim that 'a user needing bitwise identity at every rank can additionally set multithread=FALSE' for assignTaxonomy() is not fully accurate -- 2 independent single-threaded seeded assignTaxonomy() runs on the fresh slice differ at 2/770 cells (Kingdom + Order ranks only; genus 0/770 differs in every comparison run). Minor and already-adjacent to a disclosed residual, but the comment overclaims.

reliability.note: Fault Tolerance: all three stochastic methods now have documented, independently-verified set.seed() guidance, and genus-level (the rank the Skill's own claims and the veto are scoped to) results are bit-identical across every configuration tested in this re-audit, including cross-threading. One point held back for the same non-genus residual noted under functional_suitability -- disclosed but not fully resolved, and present even in the single-threaded configuration the Skill implies is a full fix.

performance_context.note: Unchanged from the prior re-audit: memory-budget warnings present for both QIIME2 fit-classifier-naive-bayes and DECIPHER LearnTaxa. No new performance issues found; this pass's own LearnTaxa() runs (18k reference, ~35 min each) are consistent with the documented memory/time expectations.

agent_usability.note: Error Prevention: the Common Errors table and DECIPHER code comments now correctly warn an agent to seed IdTaxa() and LearnTaxa(), independently confirmed effective. One point held back because the multithread=FALSE comment (see functional_suitability) could lead an agent to promise a user 'bitwise identity at every rank' that this re-audit found is not quite true, though the operative genus-level claim holds.

human_usability.note: Forgiveness: all three originally- and newly-found determinism defects (assignTaxonomy, IdTaxa flattening, IdTaxa/LearnTaxa seeding) are now documented with Common Errors rows and inline comments that were independently confirmed to work as described.

security.note: Unchanged across all four audit passes: no hardcoded credentials, no unsanitized execution of user-provided strings, no sensitive-data handling concerns.

maintainability.note: Testability: still no example anywhere in the Skill includes a self-check that a repeated run reproduces its own prior output -- the exact class of defect this Skill has now shipped three times (assignTaxonomy pre-fix, IdTaxa flattening pre-fix, IdTaxa/LearnTaxa seeding pre-fix). Open P2 from the prior re-audit, not addressed by this fix pass, does not block landing.

agent_specific.note: Idempotency: full credit. assignTaxonomy(), IdTaxa(), and LearnTaxa() are now all confirmed idempotent at the genus rank under set.seed(), independently reverified in this pass on a completely fresh 18k-sequence reference the prior three passes never touched, in both single- and multi-threaded configurations.

inputs.label: Independent determinism reconfirmation on a data slice no prior pass used -- LearnTaxa/IdTaxa seeded vs. unseeded, single- and multi-threaded
inputs.note: The central test of this re-audit. A freshly-drawn 18,000-sequence SILVA-138 subsample (seed 4242) that none of the original auditor, either fixer, or the prior re-auditor used (they used 8k/30k/60k/380k/5k draws). LearnTaxa() seeded twice: identical() trainingSets (TRUE). LearnTaxa() unseeded (negative control): different trainingSet than the seeded runs (FALSE) -- confirms the underlying stochasticity is genuinely still present in the algorithm and the seed is doing real work, not a coincidence. IdTaxa() seeded: identical() across 2 runs in multithreaded, identical() across 2 runs single-threaded, AND multithreaded output identical() to single-threaded output -- a bitwise identity guarantee stronger than the Skill claims. IdTaxa() UNSEEDED (negative control): 32/770 (4.2%) genus calls differ between 2 back-to-back unseeded runs -- consistent in magnitude with the prior re-audit's 33/770 and 23/770 findings on a completely different reference, corroborating that this is a real, reproducible-in-magnitude effect and not measurement noise from either pass.

key_strengths: Skill Veto T3 (Result Determinism), which fired on the two prior audit passes, is now genuinely closed. Independently reconfirmed on a completely fresh 18,000-sequence SILVA-138 reference (seed 4242) that no prior pass used: LearnTaxa() and IdTaxa() are both bit-identical under set.seed() -- IdTaxa() even bit-identical ACROSS single- vs. multi-threaded configurations, a stronger guarantee than the Skill claims -- while unseeded negative-control runs on the SAME fresh reference confirm the underlying stochasticity is genuinely real (32/770 genus differences, matching the prior re-audit's 33/770 and 23/770 in magnitude).

assignTaxonomy()'s genus-level determinism (the rank the Skill's own claims and the veto are scoped to) holds in every one of this re-audit's comparisons -- multithreaded-vs-multithreaded, single-threaded-vs-single-threaded, and cross-threading -- 0/770 genus differences in all cases.

This re-audit found one real, minor documentation inaccuracy (the fix log's claim that multithread=FALSE gives assignTaxonomy() full bitwise identity at every rank is not quite true -- a 2/770-cell, non-genus residual persists even single-threaded) and confirmed it is not a safety- or scope-relevant defect: it does not touch genus, is smaller than the already-disclosed residual from the first fix pass, and does not reopen the veto.

Every stochastic call in the Skill's R code was exhaustively enumerated this pass (grep across SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, and examples/) and cross-checked against DECIPHER's own installed-package documentation (Rd help text, not just the fix log's paraphrase) for LearnTaxa's '100 random subsamples' and IdTaxa's 'bootstraps' mechanisms -- no unaccounted-for stochastic call remains.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md's implied claim that multithread=FALSE gives assignTaxonomy() full bitwise identity at every rank is not quite accurate
recommendations.problem: Two independent seeded, single-threaded assignTaxonomy() runs on a fresh reference are not identical() -- 2/770 cells differ at the Kingdom and Order ranks (genus is unaffected, 0/770 differ). The DECIPHER section's assign_silva.R comment and the fix log both imply single-threading is a full fix for the small multithreaded residual the first fix pass disclosed; this re-audit shows it narrows but does not eliminate it.
recommendations.root_cause: The residual is very likely a floating-point tie-breaking or accumulation-order effect inside DADA2's C implementation of the bootstrap classifier, present (at a smaller magnitude) regardless of thread count -- the first fixer diagnosed the multithreaded case but did not test whether multithread=FALSE alone was sufficient before recommending it as a workaround.
recommendations.fix: Soften the SKILL.md comment to state the reproducibility guarantee is at the genus rank (which is what the Skill's own scope statement -- 'genus at best' -- already cares about), rather than implying multithread=FALSE gives bitwise identity at every rank including Kingdom/Phylum/Class/Order/Family. No code change needed; a one-line wording correction.

recommendations.title: No self-check anywhere in the Skill catches non-degenerate-output or run-to-run-reproducibility failures
recommendations.problem: Three real defects across four audit passes (assignTaxonomy non-determinism, DECIPHER all-NA flattening, IdTaxa/LearnTaxa non-determinism) all shipped silently -- no example script or SKILL.md guidance includes a lightweight check (e.g. 'rerun and diff', or 'assert >0 non-NA calls') that would have caught any of them before a user did. Carried forward unchanged from the prior re-audit; this fix pass did not address it (reasonably, since it was P2 not P0).
recommendations.root_cause: Examples are written to demonstrate the happy path only; none include a verification step.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'sanity-check your output' pattern to both the DADA2 and DECIPHER sections: rerun the classification once and diff, or assert a non-trivial fraction of non-NA genus calls, before trusting the result for downstream analysis.
